The bridge CLI and the from-goal.py converter leave the skill

Two cleanups, with no change to what the harness does. The bridge CLI was named in the docs, the remote agent's brief and the tests, but the harness has no rule, knob or code path for it: it runs in any profile once "sandbox": false. from-goal.py turned a make-goal contract into the team's task; nothing at run time used it, and running /goal needs only the skills knob and the generic boss.sh slash. A three-agent team (lead + 2 sealed helpers) did both in 10.2 minutes, with 0 rejected merges. All 36 test files of the repository pass on the branch (1,639 checks).

Findings

  1. My spec's grep was too broad. tests/accept/nogoal.sh refuses the word done_when anywhere, so the team renamed an unrelated local variable in report.py (done_when -> done_at). The rename is harmless and kept; it is the only code change outside the cleanup. template/harness/report.py:474
  2. A stale README sentence. README said no boss has run under /goal, but references/goal.md records the live run that did ("Goal achieved" in 21.2 min). Removed in the boss follow-up commit. README.md:80
  3. A tautological comment. The team's rewrite of the test_gateway.sh comment read "Without it (a task without task.attempted_if)". Shortened to "Without it, every statement ..." in the follow-up, with test_nogoal.sh updated to match. template/harness/test_gateway.sh:50
  4. boss.sh trust raced h1's prompt. At launch, h1's trust prompt got its keypress before it was drawn, so Claude Code exited. The boss restarted h1 and chose Yes by hand. Pre-existing; not part of this change.

Not covered

  • No real agent session was started under /goal (unchanged by this PR; references/goal.md already says so).
  • No real remote host was reached; the bridge CLI itself was not run. The monitor's verdict on a bridge command was checked with stubs.
